blocks.text: 1. Context Injection
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785440697452-921428439.png

System Prompting's closing recap pointed forward here. Context Injection covers exactly how retrieved chunks get inserted into the prompt, focusing on the precise phrasing rather than overall structure.
It covers the precise formatting and phrasing used to introduce retrieved content to the model.
2. From Assembly To Phrasing
Prompt Construction already decided where retrieved content goes structurally.
Context injection focuses on the exact wording and formatting used to introduce it.

blocks.text: 3. Introducing Context Clearly
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785440697452-97571304.png
A clear introductory phrase, like "using the following context," signals exactly what the retrieved text represents.
This removes any ambiguity about whether that text is instruction, example, or reference material.
4. Formatting Chunks Consistently
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785440697453-59638975.png
Prompt Construction covered labeling sources within the context; each injected chunk also benefits from a consistent, predictable format.
A uniform structure makes it easier for the model to parse where one chunk ends and the next begins.
5. Numbering Or Labeling Multiple Chunks
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785440697453-554618907.png
Numbering each injected chunk gives the model a simple way to reference a specific piece of context.
This is useful when the model needs to cite or compare across multiple sources.
6. Handling Empty Or Sparse Context
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785440697453-77814766.png
System Prompting covered handling missing information explicitly; the injection format similarly needs to handle the case where retrieval found nothing relevant.
An empty context section should be clearly marked rather than silently omitted.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Silently omitting the context section entirely when retrieval finds nothing can confuse the model about whether context was intentionally left out or simply forgotten, unlike an explicit marker stating none was found.

blocks.text: 7. Avoiding Injection Confusion
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785440697454-319753267.png
Prompt Construction covered separating instructions from retrieved content; poorly delimited injection risks the model treating retrieved text as an instruction.
Careful formatting prevents that confusion from happening.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A retrieved chunk containing text that resembles a command stays safely inert when wrapped in clear delimiters and an explicit "this is reference context" framing, rather than risking misinterpretation as an actual instruction.

blocks.text: 8. Testing Different Injection Formats
Context Ordering covered testing ordering choices empirically; the best injection phrasing similarly varies by model and task.
Testing different formats against real queries reveals what actually works best.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When Careful Context Injection Matters Most

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Careful Context Injection Matters Most
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785440697454-175075344.png
Multi chunk contexts needing citation or comparison need careful injection formatting.
A single, simple chunk of context, by contrast, needs only minimal formatting.
10. Worked Example
The example below demonstrates injecting multiple numbered chunks with a clear introductory phrase.

code.content:
chunks = [
    {"source": "handbook_v3", "text": "Refunds are processed within five business days."},
    {"source": "faq_page", "text": "Damaged items qualify for a full refund."},
]

def inject_context(chunks):
    # number each chunk so the model can reference it directly
    if not chunks:
        # mark the empty case explicitly instead of omitting it
        return "No relevant context was found for this query."

    intro = "Using the following numbered context passages:\n"
    formatted_chunks = []
    for i, chunk in enumerate(chunks, start=1):
        formatted_chunks.append(f"[{i}] (source: {chunk['source']}) {chunk['text']}")
    return intro + "\n".join(formatted_chunks)

injected = inject_context(chunks)
print("Injected context:\n")
print(injected)

print("\n---\n")
empty_injected = inject_context([])
print("Injected context when nothing was retrieved:\n")
print(empty_injected)

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Running this example shows each chunk numbered and labeled with its source under a clear introductory phrase, and an explicit message when no context exists at all.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Injecting retrieved content with no introductory phrase explaining what it represents.
Using inconsistent formatting across chunks, making boundaries hard for the model to parse.
Silently omitting the context section when retrieval finds nothing relevant.
Injecting raw retrieved text without delimiters, risking confusion with actual instructions.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Context injection writes the precise formatting and phrasing that introduces retrieved content.
It focuses on exact wording, distinct from prompt construction's structural placement decisions.
A clear introductory phrase signals exactly what the retrieved text represents.
Consistent formatting across chunks makes boundaries easier for the model to parse.
Numbering or labeling chunks gives the model a simple way to cite or reference specific context.
An empty context section should be explicitly marked, not silently omitted.
Careful formatting and delimiters prevent the model from confusing retrieved text with instructions.
The best injection phrasing varies by model and task, requiring real testing.
